claim: CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing was used to produce somatic mutations of OTX2 in the chick retina.
source: CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing was used to produce somatic mutations of OTX2 in the chick retina and identified similar phenotypes to those observed in human patients.
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: OTX2 mutations in chick retina identified similar phenotypes to those observed in human patients.
source: CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing was used to produce somatic mutations of OTX2 in the chick retina and identified similar phenotypes to those observed in human patients.
evidence: The study compares phenotypes between chick model and human patients.

claim: Single cell RNA sequencing was used to determine the functional consequences of OTX2 gene editing on the population of cells derived from OTX2-expressing retinal progenitor cells.
source: Single cell RNA sequencing was used to determine the functional consequences OTX2 gene editing on the population of cells derived from OTX2-expressing retinal progenitor cells.
evidence: The manuscript describes the methodology used for analysis.

claim: OTX2 is required for the generation of photoreceptors.
source: This confirmed that OTX2 is required for the generation of photoreceptors, but also for repression of specific retinal fates and alternative gene regulatory networks.
evidence: The single cell RNA sequencing analysis confirmed this requirement.

claim: OTX2 is required for repression of specific retinal fates and alternative gene regulatory networks.
source: This confirmed that OTX2 is required for the generation of photoreceptors, but also for repression of specific retinal fates and alternative gene regulatory networks.
evidence: The single cell RNA sequencing analysis revealed repression functions.

claim: OTX2 represses specific subtypes of retinal ganglion cells.
source: These include specific subtypes of retinal ganglion and horizontal cells, suggesting that in this context, OTX2 functions to repress sister cell fate choices.
evidence: The study identified specific cell types that are repressed by OTX2.

claim: OTX2 represses specific subtypes of horizontal cells.
source: These include specific subtypes of retinal ganglion and horizontal cells, suggesting that in this context, OTX2 functions to repress sister cell fate choices.
evidence: The study identified specific cell types that are repressed by OTX2.

claim: OTX2 functions to repress sister cell fate choices.
source: These include specific subtypes of retinal ganglion and horizontal cells, suggesting that in this context, OTX2 functions to repress sister cell fate choices.
evidence: The observation of specific cell fate changes suggests this repression mechanism.

claim: The vertebrate retina comprises six neuronal classes and several types of glia.
source: The vertebrate retina is a highly structured tissue comprising six neuronal classes and several types of glia.
evidence: This is established knowledge about retinal structure.

claim: The specification of retinal cell types is a dynamic process largely conserved across vertebrate species.
source: The specification of these diverse cell types is a dynamic process, largely conserved across vertebrate species, with the commitment to a final fate of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs), cone photoreceptors (PRs) and horizontal cells (HCs) in the first developmental wave, followed progressively by amacrine cells (ACs), rod PRs and bipolar cells (BCs) (Masland, 2001; Bassett and Wallace, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature on retinal development.

claim: Retinal ganglion cells, cone photoreceptors and horizontal cells are committed to their final fate in the first developmental wave.
source: The specification of these diverse cell types is a dynamic process, largely conserved across vertebrate species, with the commitment to a final fate of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs), cone photoreceptors (PRs) and horizontal cells (HCs) in the first developmental wave, followed progressively by amacrine cells (ACs), rod PRs and bipolar cells (BCs) (Masland, 2001; Bassett and Wallace, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature on retinal development.

claim: Amacrine cells, rod photoreceptors and bipolar cells are generated progressively after the first developmental wave.
source: The specification of these diverse cell types is a dynamic process, largely conserved across vertebrate species, with the commitment to a final fate of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs), cone photoreceptors (PRs) and horizontal cells (HCs) in the first developmental wave, followed progressively by amacrine cells (ACs), rod PRs and bipolar cells (BCs) (Masland, 2001; Bassett and Wallace, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature on retinal development.

claim: Müller glia are generated during the last phase of retinal development.
source: Müller glia are also generated during the last phase of retinal development, while astrocytes and the resident microglia are generated at early stages, independent of the neuronal retina, simultaneously with optic stalk formation (Kolb, 2007; Tao and Zhang, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature on retinal development.

claim: Astrocytes and resident microglia are generated at early stages, independent of the neuronal retina, simultaneously with optic stalk formation.
source: Müller glia are also generated during the last phase of retinal development, while astrocytes and the resident microglia are generated at early stages, independent of the neuronal retina, simultaneously with optic stalk formation (Kolb, 2007; Tao and Zhang, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature on retinal development.

claim: Multipotent retinal progenitor cells have the potential to give rise to all retinal cell types.
source: Initial studies using viral labeling showed that multipotent RPCs have the potential to give rise to all retinal cell types, in a mechanism that can be explained by both deterministic and probabilistic models (Turner and Cepko, 1987; Wetts and Fraser, 1988; Holt et al., 1988; Cepko et al., 1996; Vitorino et al., 2009; He et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by cited viral labeling studies.

claim: One class of restricted RPCs gives rise to all cell types except RGCs.
source: For example, one class of restricted RPCs gives rise to all cell types except RGCs (Brzezinski et al., 2011), one produces all cell types except RGCs and Müller glia (Hafler et al., 2012), and another that is largely restricted to only two cell types – cone PRs and HCs (Hafler et al., 2012; Emerson et al., 2013; Suzuki et al., 2013; Schick et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature on restricted RPCs.

claim: One class of restricted RPCs produces all cell types except RGCs and Müller glia.
source: For example, one class of restricted RPCs gives rise to all cell types except RGCs (Brzezinski et al., 2011), one produces all cell types except RGCs and Müller glia (Hafler et al., 2012), and another that is largely restricted to only two cell types – cone PRs and HCs (Hafler et al., 2012; Emerson et al., 2013; Suzuki et al., 2013; Schick et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature on restricted RPCs.

claim: One class of restricted RPCs is largely restricted to only two cell types – cone PRs and HCs.
source: For example, one class of restricted RPCs gives rise to all cell types except RGCs (Brzezinski et al., 2011), one produces all cell types except RGCs and Müller glia (Hafler et al., 2012), and another that is largely restricted to only two cell types – cone PRs and HCs (Hafler et al., 2012; Emerson et al., 2013; Suzuki et al., 2013; Schick et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature on restricted RPCs.

claim: The THRBCRM1 RPC type is defined by the activity of the cis regulatory module 1 (CRM1) of the gene THRB.
source: This last RPC type is defined by the activity of the cis regulatory module 1 (CRM1) of the gene THRB.
evidence: This is a definition based on molecular markers.

claim: The activation of the THRBCRM1 element requires the expression and direct binding of the OTX2 and ONECUT1 transcription factors.
source: Previous studies have determined that the activation of the THRBCRM1 element requires the expression and direct binding of the Orthodenticle Homeobox 2 (OTX2) and ONECUT1 transcription factors (Emerson et al., 2013; Souferi and Emerson, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by cited previous studies.

claim: Cellular and molecular changes occur during the generation of fate-restricted RPCs, but not in multipotent RPCs.
source: Moreover, a recent study has identified cellular and molecular changes that occur during the generation of these fate-restricted RPCs, but not in multipotent RPCs (Buenaventura et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a cited recent study.

claim: The roles of OTX2 and ONECUT1 in the establishment of the restricted RPC signature are not well understood.
source: However, the roles of OTX2 and ONECUT1 in the establishment of this restricted signature are not well understood.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in current knowledge.

claim: OTX2 is one of the key regulators of nervous system development.
source: OTX2 is one of the key regulators of nervous system development, as it is involved in forebrain and midbrain specification (Acampora et al., 1995; Ang et al., 1996; Simeone et al., 2002), pineal and pituitary gland development (Nishida et al., 2003; Henderson et al., 2009), as well as development of sensory structures such as the inner ear (Matsuo et al., 1995) and visual system (reviewed in Beby and Lamonerie, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple cited studies on OTX2 function.

claim: OTX2 is involved in forebrain and midbrain specification.
source: OTX2 is one of the key regulators of nervous system development, as it is involved in forebrain and midbrain specification (Acampora et al., 1995; Ang et al., 1996; Simeone et al., 2002), pineal and pituitary gland development (Nishida et al., 2003; Henderson et al., 2009), as well as development of sensory structures such as the inner ear (Matsuo et al., 1995) and visual system (reviewed in Beby and Lamonerie, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by cited studies.

claim: OTX2 is involved in pineal and pituitary gland development.
source: OTX2 is one of the key regulators of nervous system development, as it is involved in forebrain and midbrain specification (Acampora et al., 1995; Ang et al., 1996; Simeone et al., 2002), pineal and pituitary gland development (Nishida et al., 2003; Henderson et al., 2009), as well as development of sensory structures such as the inner ear (Matsuo et al., 1995) and visual system (reviewed in Beby and Lamonerie, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by cited studies.

claim: OTX2 is involved in development of sensory structures such as the inner ear.
source: OTX2 is one of the key regulators of nervous system development, as it is involved in forebrain and midbrain specification (Acampora et al., 1995; Ang et al., 1996; Simeone et al., 2002), pineal and pituitary gland development (Nishida et al., 2003; Henderson et al., 2009), as well as development of sensory structures such as the inner ear (Matsuo et al., 1995) and visual system (reviewed in Beby and Lamonerie, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by cited studies.

claim: OTX2 is involved in visual system development.
source: OTX2 is one of the key regulators of nervous system development, as it is involved in forebrain and midbrain specification (Acampora et al., 1995; Ang et al., 1996; Simeone et al., 2002), pineal and pituitary gland development (Nishida et al., 2003; Henderson et al., 2009), as well as development of sensory structures such as the inner ear (Matsuo et al., 1995) and visual system (reviewed in Beby and Lamonerie, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by cited review.

claim: During optic vesicle formation, OTX2 directs evagination of the optic vesicle to contact the surface ectoderm along with RAX, PAX6, HES1 and SIX3.
source: In the visual system, OTX2 is expressed in different subsets of cells as development progresses – first, during optic vesicle formation, OTX2 directs evagination of the optic vesicle to contact the surface ectoderm along with RAX, PAX6, HES1 and SIX3 (Adler and Canto-Soler, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a cited study.

claim: During the specification of the neuronal and retinal pigment epithelium territories, OTX2 is highly expressed in the RPE.
source: Later, during the specification of the neuronal and retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) territories, OTX2 is highly expressed in the RPE (Martinez-Morales et al., 2001) and in a subset of RPCs that primarily generate cones and HCs (Emerson and Cepko, 2011; Emerson et al., 2013; Buenaventura et al., 2018), then in postmitotic PRs during the specification of retinal neuronal cell types (Nishida et al., 2003), in the PRs and BCs in the mature retina (Koike et al., 2007; Kim et al., 2008), and in a subset of Müller glia (Brzezinski et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by cited studies.

claim: OTX2 is expressed in a subset of RPCs that primarily generate cones and HCs.
source: Later, during the specification of the neuronal and retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) territories, OTX2 is highly expressed in the RPE (Martinez-Morales et al., 2001) and in a subset of RPCs that primarily generate cones and HCs (Emerson and Cepko, 2011; Emerson et al., 2013; Buenaventura et al., 2018), then in postmitotic PRs during the specification of retinal neuronal cell types (Nishida et al., 2003), in the PRs and BCs in the mature retina (Koike et al., 2007; Kim et al., 2008), and in a subset of Müller glia (Brzezinski et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by cited studies.

claim: OTX2 is expressed in postmitotic PRs during the specification of retinal neuronal cell types.
source: Later, during the specification of the neuronal and retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) territories, OTX2 is highly expressed in the RPE (Martinez-Morales et al., 2001) and in a subset of RPCs that primarily generate cones and HCs (Emerson and Cepko, 2011; Emerson et al., 2013; Buenaventura et al., 2018), then in postmitotic PRs during the specification of retinal neuronal cell types (Nishida et al., 2003), in the PRs and BCs in the mature retina (Koike et al., 2007; Kim et al., 2008), and in a subset of Müller glia (Brzezinski et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by cited studies.

claim: OTX2 is expressed in the PRs and BCs in the mature retina.
source: Later, during the specification of the neuronal and retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) territories, OTX2 is highly expressed in the RPE (Martinez-Morales et al., 2001) and in a subset of RPCs that primarily generate cones and HCs (Emerson and Cepko, 2011; Emerson et al., 2013; Buenaventura et al., 2018), then in postmitotic PRs during the specification of retinal neuronal cell types (Nishida et al., 2003), in the PRs and BCs in the mature retina (Koike et al., 2007; Kim et al., 2008), and in a subset of Müller glia (Brzezinski et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by cited studies.

claim: OTX2 is expressed in a subset of Müller glia.
source: Later, during the specification of the neuronal and retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) territories, OTX2 is highly expressed in the RPE (Martinez-Morales et al., 2001) and in a subset of RPCs that primarily generate cones and HCs (Emerson and Cepko, 2011; Emerson et al., 2013; Buenaventura et al., 2018), then in postmitotic PRs during the specification of retinal neuronal cell types (Nishida et al., 2003), in the PRs and BCs in the mature retina (Koike et al., 2007; Kim et al., 2008), and in a subset of Müller glia (Brzezinski et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a cited study.

claim: Several studies have reported OTX2 mutations in humans with ocular malformations.
source: As a consequence of its involvement during early eye genesis, several studies have reported OTX2 mutations in humans with ocular malformations.
evidence: This is supported by multiple studies on human OTX2 mutations.

claim: Clinical manifestations of OTX2 mutations in humans range from unilateral and bilateral anophthalmia, microphthalmia, optic nerve aplasia to various forms of coloboma.
source: The clinical manifestations range from unilateral and bilateral anophthalmia, microphthalmia, optic nerve aplasia to various forms of coloboma (reviewed in Gat-Yablonski, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a cited review.

claim: Homozygous OTX2 mutants die embryonically due to defects in the specification of the anterior neuroectoderm.
source: Previous studies have examined the role of OTX2 in the development of the neuronal retina using conditional floxed mouse models, as homozygous OTX2 mutants die embryonically due to defects in the specification of the anterior neuroectoderm (Acampora et al., 1995).
evidence: This is supported by a cited study.

claim: When OTX2 loss is mediated by a post-mitotic PR Cre driver, a severe loss of PRs was observed.
source: When OTX2 loss is mediated by a post-mitotic PR Cre driver, a severe loss of PRs was observed, while the number of PAX6-positive cells was increased, suggesting a trans-differentiation of the mutant cells into amacrine-like neurons (Nishida et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by a cited study.

claim: When OTX2 loss is mediated by a post-mitotic PR Cre driver, the number of PAX6-positive cells was increased.
source: When OTX2 loss is mediated by a post-mitotic PR Cre driver, a severe loss of PRs was observed, while the number of PAX6-positive cells was increased, suggesting a trans-differentiation of the mutant cells into amacrine-like neurons (Nishida et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by a cited study.

claim: Loss of OTX2 in post-mitotic PRs suggests a trans-differentiation of the mutant cells into amacrine-like neurons.
source: When OTX2 loss is mediated by a post-mitotic PR Cre driver, a severe loss of PRs was observed, while the number of PAX6-positive cells was increased, suggesting a trans-differentiation of the mutant cells into amacrine-like neurons (Nishida et al., 2003).
evidence: This is an interpretation supported by a cited study.

claim: Microarray analysis of OTX2 mutant retinas supported the conclusion of trans-differentiation into amacrine-like neurons.
source: Microarray analysis of these retinas supported this conclusion (Omori et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a cited microarray study.

claim: When OTX2 ablation was initiated throughout the early retina, PR loss and abnormal generation of amacrine-like cells was reported.
source: Similar PR loss and abnormal generation of amacrine-like cells, along with loss of BCs and HCs was reported, when OTX2 ablation was initiated throughout the early retina (Sato et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a cited study.

claim: When OTX2 ablation was initiated throughout the early retina, loss of BCs and HCs was reported.
source: Similar PR loss and abnormal generation of amacrine-like cells, along with loss of BCs and HCs was reported, when OTX2 ablation was initiated throughout the early retina (Sato et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a cited study.

claim: OTX2 expression is initiated in specific RPC populations prior to the formation of PRs.
source: In addition, OTX2 expression is initiated in specific RPC populations prior to the formation of PRs and this expression would not be compromised by the previously used PR Cre drivers (Emerson et al., 2013; Buenaventura et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by cited studies.

claim: The functional role of OTX2 in the RPC population that will generate PRs is unknown.
source: Thus, the functional role of OTX2 in this RPC population that will generate PRs is unknown.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in knowledge.

claim: Two RNA guides corresponding to mRNA positions 141 and 167 in the coding sequence of the OTX2 gene were used to generate mutations.
source: To generate mutations that disrupt the function of the OTX2 gene, two RNA guides that corresponded to mRNA positions 141 and 167 in the coding sequence of the OTX2 gene, called guide 2 (g2) and guide 3 (g3), were used (Figure 1A–B).
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental design and refers to Figure 1A-B.

claim: A DNA plasmid encoding one of the guides and an encoded source of Cas9 was co-electroporated with a fluorescent reporter into chick retinas.
source: In all experiments, a DNA plasmid (plasmid p18) encoding one of these guides and an encoded source of Cas9 was co-electroporated with a fluorescent reporter into several stages of chick retinas, either in ovo or ex vivo, and analyzed at specific stages (Figure 1C–E).
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental procedure and refers to Figure 1C-E.

claim: In ovo electroporation at E1.5 targeting the right eye yielded severe anatomical defects of the electroporated eye upon analysis at E5.
source: In ovo electroporation was first used at E1.5 (HH9-HH11), targeting only the right eye of each embryo. Electroporation of the OTX2 g2 or g3 yielded severe anatomical defects of the electroporated eye upon analysis at E5, a timepoint when both the neuronal retina and the RPE territories have already been specified (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–H).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results and refers to figures.

claim: Morphological defects observed in the OTX2CRISPR mutants ranged from microphthalmia, patches of depigmentation in the RPE, defects of the optic nerve, and coloboma-like phenotypes.
source: The morphological defects observed in the OTX2CRISPR mutants ranged from microphthalmia (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C,E,I), patches of depigmentation in the RPE (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–H), defects of the optic nerve (ON), such as ON head enlargement, as well as both iridial and optic stalk coloboma-like phenotypes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D,E,F,H).
evidence: The manuscript describes observed phenotypes and refers to figures.

claim: The left eye, not targeted by electroporation, developed normally as expected.
source: For all in ovo experiments the left eye, not targeted by electroporation, developed normally as expected (MGT).
evidence: The manuscript describes control observations.

claim: The RPE layer in OTX2CRISPR mutants was found to contain structures composed of cells that were depigmented, enlarged, intensely GFP-positive, and OTX2-negative.
source: The RPE layer was found to contain structures composed of cells that were depigmented, enlarged, intensely GFP-positive, and OTX2-negative (Figure 1F,G).
evidence: The manuscript describes immunofluorescence observations and refers to figures.

claim: These RPE structures in OTX2CRISPR mutants were absent in CTRL retinas.
source: These structures were absent in CTRL retinas and were largely EdU and PH3-negative, with low expression levels of VSX2 and high levels of PAX6 (Figure 1H,I, Figure 1—figure supplement 1K–P).
evidence: The manuscript describes comparative observations and refers to figures.

claim: The OTX2CRISPR mutants displayed varying degrees of effects on OTX2 expression, ranging from absence of the outer OTX2 population to complete loss of OTX2 throughout the entire retina.
source: The OTX2CRISPR mutants displayed varying degrees of effects on OTX2 expression, ranging from absence of the outer OTX2 population to complete loss of OTX2 throughout the entire retina (Figure 1G).
evidence: The manuscript describes observed phenotypic variation and refers to a figure.

claim: When mutant retinas were analyzed at E6, the GFP-positive cells generally lack OTX2 protein.
source: When mutant retinas were analyzed at E6, the analyzed regions of the retina have many OTX2-positive cells, however, the GFP-positive cells generally lack OTX2 protein (Figure 1K).
evidence: The manuscript describes immunofluorescence observations and refers to a figure.

claim: The absence of OTX2-positive cells in the mutant was more pronounced at E10.
source: The absence of OTX2-positive cells in the mutant was more pronounced at E10, when the retina is layered, and the OTX2-positive PRs are concentrated in the ONL and BCs are located in the outer part on the INL (Figure 1L).
evidence: The manuscript describes temporal observations and refers to a figure.

claim: Columns of GFP-positive cells that lack OTX2 form gaps within the OTX2-positive populations in the ONL and INL at E10.
source: Columns of GFP-positive cells that lack OTX2 form gaps within the OTX2-positive populations in the ONL and INL (Figure 1M).
evidence: The manuscript describes spatial observations and refers to a figure.

claim: OTX2 g2 guided-Cas9 is able to disrupt OTX2 expression and leads to underrepresentation of PR and BC fates in the electroporated population.
source: These experiments suggest that OTX2 g2 guided-Cas9 is able to disrupt OTX2 expression and leads to underrepresentation of PR and BC fates in the electroporated population, in agreement with a previous study in mice (Nishida et al., 2003; Koike et al., 2007).
evidence: The manuscript interprets experimental results and cites supporting studies.

claim: Immunofluorescence examination of retinas revealed a qualitative decrease in OTX2-positive cells in the electroporated population.
source: Immunofluorescence examination of retinas revealed a qualitative decrease in OTX2-positive cells in the electroporated population (arrows in Figure 2A–B).
evidence: The manuscript describes immunofluorescence observations and refers to figures.

claim: In the OTX2CRISPR mutants, an approximately 50% reduction in the percentage of OTX2-positive cells within the electroporated population was detected using two different OTX2 antibodies.
source: In the OTX2CRISPR mutants, an approximately 50% reduction in the percentage of OTX2-positive cells within the electroporated population was detected using two different OTX2 antibodies (Figure 2C–D, Supplementary file 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: The manuscript describes quantitative flow cytometry results and refers to figures.

claim: In OTX2CRISPR mutants, an almost two-fold increase in the percentage of PAX6-positive cells was detected as compared to controls.
source: In OTX2CRISPR mutants, an almost two-fold increase in the percentage of PAX6-positive cells was detected as compared to controls (Figure 2E–F, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: The manuscript describes quantitative flow cytometry results and refers to figures.

claim: OTX2CRISPR mutant retinas had a significant reduction in THRBCRM2 activity.
source: OTX2CRISPR mutant retinas had a significant reduction in THRBCRM2 activity (Figure 2G–H, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: The manuscript describes quantitative results and refers to figures.

claim: The OTX2ECR2 enhancer element is active in OTX2-positive RPCs in the chicken retina.
source: To do this, the previously reported OTX2ECR2 enhancer element (Figure 3A), which is active in OTX2-positive RPCs in the chicken retina, was used (Emerson and Cepko, 2011).
evidence: The manuscript describes a previously reported tool and cites the source.

claim: In CTRL retinas, GFP expression driven by the OTX2ECR2 enhancer's activity is observed predominately in the outer retina/PR layer.
source: In CTRL retinas, upon electroporation at E5 and two days in culture, GFP expression driven by the enhancer's activity is observed predominately in the outer retina/PR layer, with fewer cells, showing less intense GFP expression, in the inner retina (Figure 3B).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental observations and refers to a figure.

claim: The OTX2ECR2 enhancer's activity co-localizes primarily with OTX2-positive retinal cells electroporated at E5 and cultured for 2 days.
source: The enhancer's activity, observed by GFP expression, co-localizes primarily with OTX2-positive retinal cells electroporated at E5 and cultured for 2 days, consistent with previous observations (Emerson and Cepko, 2011).
evidence: The manuscript describes observations consistent with cited previous work.

claim: In vivo experiments have demonstrated that OTX2ECR2 drove reporter activity in both PRs and LHX1-positive HCs and very rarely targeted POU4F1-positive RGCs.
source: In vivo experiments have demonstrated that OTX2ECR2 drove reporter activity in both PRs and LHX1-positive HCs and very rarely targeted POU4F1-positive RGCs (Emerson and Cepko, 2011).
evidence: The manuscript cites previous in vivo experimental results.

claim: Characterization of OTX2ECR2 reporter activity in the OTX2CRISPR retinas shows a qualitative shift in the cell populations with a dramatic reduction in the PR population.
source: Characterization of OTX2ECR2 reporter activity in the OTX2CRISPR retinas shows a qualitative shift in the cell populations – a dramatic reduction in the PR population as well as an increase in the inner retina population with many more intensely labeled GFP-positive cells (Figure 3C–D).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental observations and refers to figures.

claim: Characterization of OTX2ECR2 reporter activity in the OTX2CRISPR retinas shows an increase in the inner retina population with many more intensely labeled GFP-positive cells.
source: Characterization of OTX2ECR2 reporter activity in the OTX2CRISPR retinas shows a qualitative shift in the cell populations – a dramatic reduction in the PR population as well as an increase in the inner retina population with many more intensely labeled GFP-positive cells (Figure 3C–D).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental observations and refers to figures.

claim: 73% of OTX2ECR2::GFP-positive cells were also OTX2-positive in control samples.
source: To confirm previously reported estimates of the activity of the OTX2ECR2 element in OTX2-positive cells, a quantitative flow cytometry analysis was performed. 73% (c.i. ±2.4%) of GFP-positive cells were also OTX2-positive.
evidence: The manuscript describes quantitative flow cytometry results.

claim: In OTX2CRISPR mutants, OTX2ECR2::GFP-positive cells were positive for OTX2 protein in only 22% of the g2 cells and in 15% of g3 cells.
source: In contrast to CTRL samples, OTX2ECR2::GFP-positive cells in OTX2CRISPR mutants were positive for OTX2 protein in only 22% (c.i. ±5.9%) of the g2 cells and in 15% (c.i. ±8.1) of g3 cells (Figure 3E–G, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: The manuscript describes quantitative flow cytometry results and refers to figures.

claim: There is a robust increase in both the number and the intensity of the signal in the GFP-only population in OTX2CRISPR mutants.
source: In addition, there is a robust increase in both the number and the intensity of the signal in the GFP-only population (green box), suggesting that these are the newly generated, mutant cells (Figure 3E).
evidence: The manuscript describes flow cytometry observations and refers to a figure.

claim: Cell suspensions of dissociated retinas were processed for single cell library preparation using a 10X Genomics Chromium Single Cell 3' platform.
source: Cell suspensions of dissociated retinas were processed for single cell library preparation using a 10X Genomics Chromium Single Cell 3' platform (Zheng et al., 2017) and sequenced on an Illumina HiSeq 4000 sequencer.
evidence: The manuscript describes the methodology used.

claim: Cells from three retinas of embryos PCR-identified as female were pooled per sample.
source: Prior to retinal dissociation, the embryos were genotyped for sex determination (Methods) and cells from three retinas of embryos PCR-identified as female were pooled per sample.
evidence: The manuscript describes the sample preparation procedure.

claim: For each of the mutant retinas included in the sample, the contralateral eye was used as a CTRL sample to limit the variability across individual animals.
source: For each of the mutant retinas included in the sample, the contralateral eye was used as a CTRL sample to limit the variability across individual animals.
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental design.

claim: Examination of the sequencing reads using the Integrative Genomics Viewer shows a wide degree of mutation present at the Cas9 target location in the OTX2CRISPR sample.
source: Examination of the sequencing reads using the Integrative Genomics Viewer - IGV (Robinson et al., 2011) shows a wide degree of mutation present at that location in the OTX2CRISPR sample that is consistent with repair through the NHEJ pathway (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The manuscript describes sequencing analysis results and refers to a figure.

claim: Deep sequencing showed that the majority of reads in the OTX2CRISPR cells contained a mutation localized to the targeted region with only 28.69% of reads containing a wildtype sequence.
source: Deep sequencing showed that the majority of reads in the OTX2CRISPR cells contained a mutation localized to the targeted region with only 28.69% of reads containing a wildtype sequence (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: The manuscript describes amplicon sequencing results and refers to a figure.

claim: The CTRL samples contained 97.97% wildtype sequence.
source: In contrast, the CTRL samples contained 97.97% wildtype sequence.
evidence: The manuscript describes amplicon sequencing results for control samples.

claim: More than 40% of the mutations are expected to lead to truncation of the protein within the homeodomain.
source: Therefore, more than 40% of the mutations are expected to lead to truncation of the protein within the homeodomain and the remainder to alter the sequence in the homeodomain.
evidence: The manuscript interprets the mutation distribution data.

claim: Ten different clusters were identified in the CTRL OTX2ECR2 lineage based on previously characterized markers.
